overall: The intended message is delivered: literature and language reach people through collaborative work; preservation keeps those encounters possible; sustainable livelihoods require practical arrangements rather than admiration alone. No material factual blocker identified in this bounded pass. This is not a re-verification of every source claim.

findings.kind: evidence gap; later research, not factual correction
findings.excerpt: Pattanayak asked that the royalties go to the Krishnamurthy Foundation.
findings.reader_impact: The opening demonstrates a film-to-reader-to-new-edition encounter, but cannot establish that adaptation fees or book-sales growth sustained the novelist. This remains the largest unanswered element of the author’s livelihood question.
findings.recommendation: Retain the present precise NBT publishing context. Do not insert a compensation claim. The next worthwhile research is one author/producer/publisher account documenting permission, credited contribution and actual compensation or identifiable edition sales; do not repeat the exhausted searches without a new source.

findings.excerpt: Pranab and Sikandar share one song; Chitta and Susheela another.
findings.reader_impact: The same Mamata credits recur shortly afterward in Prafulla’s soundtrack section and Pranab’s composer section. The hub then also previews the Urdu-learning and Tapu choices that open their dedicated profiles, reducing discovery across consecutive chapters.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hub’s two-song ensemble map. In Prafulla retain the distinct third song and composer-performing example; shorten the repeated two-song credits to one connective sentence. In Pranab retain the first-person learning story and Jajabara recording; link back to Mamata instead of listing the full credits again. Shorten the hub’s Urdu-learning and Tapu interview previews rather than cut the fuller profiles.

findings.excerpt: A reader can linger over a narrator’s irony.
findings.reader_impact: Several adjacent writer profiles explain the same prose-to-performance contrast with hypothetical pauses, voices and camera attention. These are reasonable interpretations, but repeated explanations can displace the writers’ specific work.
findings.recommendation: Keep the full adaptation explanation in the literature bridge. Let Gopal’s Sova notice, actual radio programme and recordings do more of the narrative work; shorten this generic paragraph. Similarly trim Manglu’s hypothetical line/pause/camera comparison rather than add length.

findings.kind: thin literary encounter; optional later research
findings.section: A place, and a life of writing
findings.excerpt: These titles open a larger writing life beyond the familiar connection between Biswal and *Bhukha*.
findings.reader_impact: The profile establishes a wider bibliography and teacher identity, but offers little of the language or lived working practice behind them. Generic reflections on children’s writing fill space without a named children’s text.
findings.recommendation: Do not invent a classroom memory or assume a teaching-income history. If an authorized excerpt or participant account becomes available, replace one generic paragraph with a precise short reading or documented working episode. The current concise profile can stand meanwhile; do not add a further biography.

findings.excerpt: Mohanty’s place in this story begins with the page.
findings.reader_impact: The invitation to return to the novels is less immediately usable than Basanta’s direct translated-story links and Kalindi’s identified editions. Its source list mainly leads to biography/film credits.
findings.recommendation: When a reliable publisher/library edition is identified, add one compact reading route for Kaa or another discussed novel, distinguishing catalogue from readable text. Until then do not imply the film or full novel is freely available. This is an access improvement, not a publication blocker.

findings.excerpt: The books ask different questions: what followed what, who participated, and how audiences encountered the films.
findings.reader_impact: The guide responsibly discloses limited reading, but a new reader must work through many entries before deciding where to begin. More titles would worsen the problem.
findings.recommendation: Add a short choose-your-question orientation using existing entries only: chronology—Ghosh/Rath; social questions—Sanjoy Patnaik; songs—Deo/Chhotray; first-person working lives—memoirs. Retain edition/access qualifications beside the affected entries; do not describe unread arguments.

findings.excerpt: I began by asking how to put money in a writer’s pocket. I am still following that question.
findings.reader_impact: The intent is compelling, but a reader chiefly interested in practical livelihoods passes through fourteen readings before the first overview and many more before economics. The literary sequence is coherent; it need not be reordered.
findings.recommendation: Offer a compact optional reading path near the introduction or contents: literature bridge → one writer → one film → economics/futures. Reuse existing reading-path support; preserve the author’s personal wording and the full sequence.

what_already_works: The introduction explicitly limits the book’s historical ambition and avoids promising income from adaptation.
Basanta and Kalindi establish literary lives beyond film; translators, publishers and screenplay writers receive distinct credit.
Manglu and Bhukha preserve Sambalpuri specificity rather than silently treating every regional work as Odia-language cinema.
Music makes collaboration audible through named recording roles; Tapu is presented through choices rather than only loss or family.
Memory and Discovery already answers the earlier archive gap with collectors, institutions, access and paid skilled work; another generic preservation article is unnecessary.
Surya and Sita accounts resist recovery/restoration/completion conflations.
do_not_reopen_without_new_source: Adaptation payment terms and unsupported book-sales causation
Doctorate details or a consultation with Surya Deo not documented in the records
recommended_priority_order: Reduce the compact music cluster duplication.
Trim repeated generic adaptation explanations while preserving each distinctive example.
Offer the short optional livelihood reading path without disrupting the literary sequence.
Treat actual adaptation compensation and a close reading of Manglu as future evidence work, not placeholders to fill now.
limits: No external browsing; retained records reused, no new factual claims introduced.
No demand for encyclopedic contributor coverage, fresh biographies or an exhaustive bibliography.
Style recommendations are editorial judgments, explicitly separate from factual correction.
